lessons: Filament length measured from the right electrode can include growth within or along the electrode edge, so tip position relative to both electrodes should be checked directly before claiming a filament bridged the gap.

Lithium plating in this cross-section appears as a pale fringe on the separator-facing graphite surface, so onset should be bracketed between the last clean frame and the first fringed frame rather than timed from a single frame.
The movie clock bound of about twenty minutes is too coarse to prove a precise plating onset or growth speed, so video timing should be compared to the voltage log only within that bound.

Filament length measured from one electrode can include a merged outline with the far electrode, so tip position relative to both electrode edges should be checked directly before claiming a filament bridged the gap.

Plating markers (time into each charge): cycle 1 charge (2 mA/cm2): voltage first goes below 0 V vs Li/Li+ after 7.43 h +/-0.68 h assuming voltage error within +/-10 mV (accuracy not stated; -0.0 mV logged) — m_5a9153faeb34; cycle 1 charge (2 mA/cm2): voltage first comes within 5 mV of the final-hour median (-0.04681 V) and stays in that band for at least 30 min (an operational plateau definition) after 10.21 h +/-10.21 h assuming voltage error within +/-10 mV (accuracy not stated; -41.8 mV logged) — m_aefb71eaaf6d; cycle 1 charge (2 mA/cm2): voltage reaches its lowest value in this charge after 11.44 h +/-2.46 h assuming voltage error within +/-10 mV (accuracy not stated; -51.8 mV logged) — m_844e6f4c83ca; cycle 2 charge (4 mA/cm2): voltage first goes below 0 V vs Li/Li+ after 0.22 h +/-0.03 h assuming voltage error within +/-10 mV (accuracy not stated; -0.0 mV logged) — m_28a313037283; cycle 2 charge (4 mA/cm2): voltage first comes within 5 mV of the final-hour median (-0.04634 V) and stays in that band for at least 30 min (an operational plateau definition) after 4.87 h +/-4.87 h assuming voltage error within +/-10 mV (accuracy not stated; -51.3 mV logged) — m_02f8b36d8a32; cycle 2 charge (4 mA/cm2): voltage reaches its lowest value in this charge after 0.81 h +/-0.42 h assuming voltage error within +/-10 mV (accuracy not stated; -102.9 mV logged) — m_8eb9d57f2585. The stated 10 h onset can't be reconciled under the assumptions that onset = first 0 V crossing and voltage error is within +/-10 mV: its time window still lies before 9.5 h. The logged 5 mV plateau is an operational definition, with no precise physical onset established at this voltage accuracy. Cycle 2 is in the log, not in this movie. The full source log is retained for computation; the returned series keeps one sample per minute.

# extract value and uncertainty generically
def val(d):
    if isinstance(d, dict):
        if 'value' in d: return d['value']
        # nested?
        for v in d.values():
            if isinstance(v,(int,float)): return v
    return float(d)
def unc(d):
    if isinstance(d, dict):
        u=d.get('uncertainty')
        if isinstance(u, dict) and u.get('value') is not None: return u['value']

data.answer: During the first charge at 2 mA/cm2, the cell voltage first drops below 0 V after about 7.4 hours of charging (claim_29f4e853f8). That measured crossing is about 2.6 hours before the stated 10-hour onset, so under the assumptions that onset means the first 0 V crossing and that voltage error is within ±10 mV, the two cannot be reconciled (claim_0af13c8221). This voltage result alone does not show what lithium did on the surface.
data.not_proven: A precise visual plating onset was not proven: no distinct silver-grey layer separate from the gold lithiation colour was clearly bracketed between a last clean frame and a first coated frame, and the movie clock bound of about ±20 minutes is too coarse for a precise onset. The later voltage-plateau time near 10.2 hours is also too uncertain at the stated voltage accuracy to settle whether the paper's 10 h statement referred to that plateau rather than the first 0 V crossing.
